answer: Sybil resistance via scarce bandwidth-shard leasing. A rotating quorum signs a beacon naming each epoch's shard-lease map. Each identity holds one non-transferable lease, auctioned at p = base * n (n = active identities), so marginal cost rises linearly with n. Relays drop off-map attestations; leases self-revoke after two missed pings. Scarcity bars splitting one lease into parallel identities or pre-farming, and an island relay mirrors the map against rewrite. A yarrow-seed bond, unique per identity, burns on cross-shard double-signing. Cost is priced and linear in n.
